plan.title: Psoriasis lesional vs control: TPM-only DE + functional context
plan.analytical_narrative: The core delivered only a gene-level TPM table (12000 genes x 12 samples, Salmon output) plus a 2-column metadata sheet — no raw counts, no quantification directories. Count-based DE tools (DESeq2, edgeR, pydeseq2) require raw counts for their negative-binomial dispersion model and cannot be validly applied to TPM; using them here would silently produce meaningless variance estimates. The correct substitute is limma's empirical-Bayes moderated t-test on log2(TPM+1) (limma-trend), which borrows information across genes to remain usable at n=6 vs 6, unpaired, single batch. Track 1 first verifies sample-condition alignment and filters unexpressed genes (QC), then runs limma-trend as the primary DE test with a nonparametric Wilcoxon cross-check given the small per-group n. Track 2 uses the same TPM matrix — the native unit for rank-based deconvolution — to characterize immune/epidermal compositional shifts known to accompany psoriasis, giving context for whether DE genes reflect within-cell-type reprogramming or bulk-tissue composition change. Track 3 takes the DE gene list forward into WikiPathways/Hallmark enrichment and a STRING PPI hub-gene analysis, both organism-matched (human) references confirmed present in /mnt/refs, to move from a gene list to prioritized, interpretable biology.
